# Umber strategy review: the P0/P1 claim against the code, 2026-10-12

**Bottom line:** the engine crates are real. The product loop on top of them is broken: what you paint can't be seen in 3D, can't be undone, isn't saved, and takes no pen pressure. The P0 floor is not met.

---

## 1. GAPS: rows marked ✓ that have holes you can name

**[critical] The 3D viewport never shows paint.** All four 3D view modes render a constant gray mesh.
- Evidence:
  - The mesh pass's vertex input is only position and normal, with no UV attribute (`crates/umber-gpu/src/shaders.rs:120-122`).
  - Base color is a hardcoded constant: `const BASE_COLOR = (0.72, 0.72, 0.75)` (`shaders.rs:145`).
  - The OpenPBR pass binds only the camera and a uniform parameter block (`shaders.rs:482-483`).
  - `docs/perf/protocol.md:85` admits it: "the mesh pass has no texture binding yet."
  - Rows this undermines: §5:77 (OpenPBR viewport), §5:79 (view modes, "texture bindings follow-up"), §5:87 (perf floor), and §1:29 (3D stroke evaluation: you paint in 3D but can't see the result there).
- Fix:
  1. Add UV to `VertexInput`.
  2. Bind the per-tile channel textures from `PaintState` into the mesh pass (one bind group per UDIM tile).
  3. Drive OpenPBR from sampled textures instead of the uniform.
  4. Add a golden test: paint a dab, render the viewport, assert the texel color appears.

**[critical] The live paint target is 512², not 4K.**
- Evidence:
  - `const TARGET_SIZE: u32 = 512;` with the comment "Wave 2: single square tile" (`crates/umber-app/src/paint_state.rs:180`).
  - §2:43 claims "4K default in paint stack."
  - The 4K and 8K runs only happen through a test hook (`paint_state.rs:937`). In the real app, "8K export" (§6:99) is a 16× upsample of 512².
- Fix: make target size a per-texture-set setting with a 4096 default, routed through the tile pool. Re-run the stroke soak at that size and record it in the baseline table.

**[critical] Brush strokes have no undo.**
- Evidence:
  - `paint_state.rs:445-447`: "a paint-tool stroke ends the retouch history (v1 — paint strokes have no undo of their own yet)."
  - Ctrl+Z only reverts `LayerCommand`s (`document.rs:25`) and smudge/clone strokes.
  - The §12 undo-RAM "baseline" measures metadata bytes; `protocol.md:102` says so itself.
- Fix: extend the dirty-rect snapshots the retouch history already takes so they cover every stroke (paint, erase, fill, path), under one budget. This is the existing `UndoStack<PaintStrokeCommand>` widened, not new architecture.

**[critical] Painted pixels are not saved.**
- Evidence:
  - `save_project` (`main.rs:638-689`) writes the layer stack metadata, display settings, the graph `.mtlx` and the journal sequence number. It never reads back the paint target or writes it to `AssetStore`.
  - `open_project` (`main.rs:698-760`) restores only the stack and the graph; there's no `WriteRegion` reload.
  - So save → quit → reopen loses all paint. §8:120-122 ("textures as content-hash tiles", "save→load→export identical bytes") holds only for JSON. The round-trip tests (`project.rs:665`, `:703`) never touch pixels.
- Fix: on save, read back each tile and store it as a content-hash PNG/EXR referenced from the paint layer; on open, upload it again. Add an app-level test: paint → save → fresh `PaintState` → load → byte-compare the readback.

**[critical] Pen pressure never reaches the brush.**
- Evidence:
  - `begin_stroke` hardcodes pressure 1.0 (`paint_state.rs:404-405`), and the UV view calls the unstyled path (`uv_view.rs:320-322`).
  - The `stylus` crate is a dependency (`umber-app/Cargo.toml:24`) with zero `stylus::` uses in umber-app.
  - The crate itself is 335 lines: an event vocabulary plus a Windows Ink skeleton. There's no Wintab, no Wayland, no X11 (`crates/stylus/src/`).
  - Rows this undermines: §1:16 (pressure dynamics: the curve model is fed a constant), §10:142 (✓ "pressure into paint pipeline"), §12:164 (input-to-photon is measured with synthetic events).
- Fix, in order:
  1. Wire the Windows Ink backend into the eframe event loop and feed `begin_stroke_styled` with real pressure.
  2. Add Linux pressure via winit 0.30's touch `force` as a stopgap.
  3. Open Wintab, Wayland and X11 as real rows, not ✓.

**[critical] Only base color can be painted.**
- Evidence:
  - There's one RGBA8 `PaintThread` per UDIM tile (`paint_state.rs:218`), keyed by tile, with no layer or channel mapping (a grep for `layer_id` in paint_state finds nothing).
  - Export pulls only `painted_base_color_tile` (`export_dialog.rs:736`).
  - Roughness, metallic, height, normal and emissive can't be painted. Every paint layer shares one surface, so the layer stack, per-channel blending (§2:38) and masks (§2:40, "metadata model") are a model with no pixels behind it.
  - The §2:36 channel stack (P0) is therefore unmet. Material painting is the Painter workflow.
- Fix: one GPU target per (layer, channel, tile) in the tile pool, plus a GPU compositor pass that implements the existing `BlendMode::composite_channel` math (`layers.rs:276`) over the stack. The brush writes one dab to every enabled channel. This is the largest piece of work in this review, and it is the product.

**[major] Rows marked ✓ whose own text admits a gap.** Quote the row against itself:
- §5:81 camera: "ortho pending." A grep finds no orthographic code.
- §5:87 perf floor: "the floor itself = the nightly perf run." But `perf/baseline.json`, which `perf-nightly.yml:49` compares against, doesn't exist, and the ref-scene column in `protocol.md:102` reads "—".
- §2:40 masks: "metadata model."
- §11:155 history: "record_context wiring = the named follow-up."
- Fix: un-tick these rows, or move the open part into its own unmarked row.

**[major] P0 rows still unmarked, yet the floor is called closed.**
- Evidence:
  - §9:130 OCIO is P0: umber-color has `default = []`, so it's stub-only.
  - §10:141 stylus is P0.
  - §10:146 distribution: there's no MSI, Flatpak or AppImage. `dist-workspace.toml:9` has `installers = ["shell", "powershell"]`.
  - STATE.md:71 says "THE P0 FLOOR CLOSED: all 57 rows built."
- Fix: correct the STATE claim, and treat these three rows as release blockers or explicitly re-tier them in DECISIONS.md.

**[major] Golden-image coverage misses the surfaces SPEC requires it for.**
- Evidence:
  - The `golden::` harness is used only in `renderer.rs`, `texture_display.rs` and `postfx_viewport.rs`.
  - SPEC.md:42-45 requires golden tests for seam strokes, layer composites and bakes. None of those exist.
- Fix: add three golden fixtures (seam stroke, two-layer composite, AO bake of the test mesh), committed and checked against lavapipe and WARP tolerance.

**[minor] STATE.md contradicts itself.** The status line reads "wave 3 of 6" (`STATE.md:7`), the "Wave 0 … DO NOT start Wave 1" handoff text (`:73`) is still live, and the handoff (`:71`) says everything is done. Fix: rewrite STATE.md from scratch around current truth.

**What's solid:** the bake engine (8 bakers, CPU+GPU tests), the export driver (two-pass, no partial writes, packing and normal conventions), the `.umber` JSON layer, and the HDR row's honest boundary proven in-module.

---

## 2. RISKS: the top 5 for a shippable v0.1.0, plus the checklist audit

1. **[critical] Ticks recorded faster than features got exercised.**
   - Evidence: 297 commits in 4 days (132 on 10-09 alone). The ✓ marks are self-written per kill. There's no recorded interactive verification; the GUI roadmap's own success test, the "next to Substance Painter on a 4K screen" screenshot (`gui-audit-and-roadmap.md:279`), was never run. SPEC's W5 dogfood gate ("≥2 external artists complete a full asset", SPEC.md:65) never happened.
   - Fix: no ✓ without a user-path test or a recorded manual run (a video or screenshot attached to the commit).
2. **[critical] The core loop is a scaffold.** The six criticals in §1 all sit on one path: import → paint → see → undo → save → export. Each subsystem passes its own tests, but the joins between them don't exist. Fix: §4's core-loop phase.
3. **[major] The per-layer, per-channel tile pool and GPU compositor don't exist, and they're the hard part.**
   - Evidence: `architecture.md:76-82` names virtual texturing and the per-dirty-tile compositor as "the hard 20%". The app has one 512² RGBA8 surface per tile.
   - Moving to 4K × 8 channels × N layers is about 64 MB per layer-channel per tile at 4K RGBA8; RGBA16F (§2:47 formats) doubles it. That will collide with the undo budget and VRAM on the reference GPU class.
   - Fix: prototype the memory model before writing more features, and measure VRAM at 10 layers × 5 channels × 4K.
4. **[major] The OCIO P0 row depends on a C++ build that has never run.** DECISIONS.md:83-88 keeps it manual-dispatch, and the "revisit when the display panel ships" trigger already fired (956ecdd). Fix: run the bundled build once in CI on both OSes now; if it fails, take the documented baked-LUT fallback and re-scope §9:130.
5. **[major] Bus factor and an unratified contract.** SPEC.md:117 `[ ] SPEC v1.0 RATIFIED` is still unchecked. Every P0/P1 claim is measured against a draft. SPEC.md:95 names funding and a second maintainer as the biggest risk, and nothing has addressed it. Fix: ratify (or edit) the SPEC before tagging, and recruit the dogfood cohort.

**Release checklist audit (`docs/specs/release-checklist-0.1.0.md`):**
- **[critical] Every gate checks process; none checks function.** Gates 1-5 are "assembled", CI, changelog, marks and baselines. Nothing requires the app to do the job. Fix: add a Gate 0 journey test, run manually on Windows and Linux:
  1. Import an FBX.
  2. Paint with pressure at 4K into base color and roughness.
  3. See it lit in 3D.
  4. Undo and redo.
  5. Save, quit, reopen, and see the pixels still there.
  6. Export Unreal ORM and decode-verify the packed channels.
- **[major] It's stale and contradicts requirements.md.** Gate 1 still reads `[IN FLIGHT]` (`:11`), and the known-deferred list (`:38-40`) names path tools and postfx, which requirements.md marks ✓ (§1:26, §5:84).
- **[major] It defers a P0 row.** OCIO sits under "known-deferred" (`:39`) while §9:130 is P0. A "P0 floor" gate can't pass with a P0 deferred.
- **[major] The tag message promises installers the dist config can't produce.** It says "installers for Linux + Windows" (`:31`), but there's no MSI, Flatpak or AppImage. Either add them to `dist-workspace.toml` (cargo-dist supports `msi`) or change the message to "archives + install scripts."
- **[minor] Gate 5 can't pass as written.** `perf/baseline.json` is missing, so `perf-nightly.yml:49` has nothing to compare against.

---

## 3. EXPANSIONS: absent from the table, needed for a credible v0.1

| Feature | Section | Priority | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Color picker with eyedropper (screen and texture sample), HSV/hex, swatches | §11 | P0 | You can't paint without picking color. The GUI roadmap has it in Phase 2; it should be a requirements row. |
| ID-map / mesh-map mask selection (click a color in the ID bake → mask) | §2 | P0 | It's how Painter, ArmorPaint and 3DCoat users mask every asset, and the ID baker is already built. |
| Layer effects/filter stack (generators, levels, blur and HSL on a layer or mask) | §2 | P0 | Smart masks (§4:68) need somewhere to live non-destructively, and "mask stacks with effects" (§2:40) has no effect list. |
| Stencil / decal projection (screen-space image stamped onto the mesh) | §1 | P0 | Decals and photo-sourcing are daily work in all three competitors. |
| Multi-texture-set documents (more than one material on one mesh) | §2 | P0 | Most real game assets have several materials, and `document.rs:21-22` is single-set. §2:36 assumes multi-set but nothing tracks it. |
| Material painting (one stroke deposits color + roughness + metal + height) | §1 | P0 | Painter's core interaction. It belongs as its own explicit row so it can't be ticked by base-color painting. |
| Layer and mask thumbnails | §11 | P1 | You can't navigate a 20-layer stack blind. Phase 1 kill 1 claimed this infrastructure; verify it landed. |
| Height → normal in the viewport (height channel shading the normal live) | §5 | P0 | Height painting is invisible without it, and it's a cheap shader derivative. |
| Material/asset browser shelf (materials, brushes, alphas, smart materials as thumbnails) | §11 | P1 | §11:153 lists "assets/shelf" but no row defines its content or thumbnails. |
| Shortcut map + remapping, and a brush-size/hardness drag hotkey (Ctrl+drag style) | §11 | P1 | Artists drive the tool from the keyboard and pen. Phase 0b's "9 shortcuts" is too thin. |
| Mesh UV validation / overlap warning at import | §7 | P1 | Overlapping UVs silently corrupt paint and bakes. 3DCoat and Painter both warn. |
| Lights and a material preview sphere / environment rotation hotkey | §5 | P1 | You judge PBR by turning the light (Shift+drag in Painter). |

---

## 4. IMPROVEMENTS to the plan itself

1. **[critical] Put a "core loop" phase before GUI Phase 0b and all P2 work.** CLAUDE.md names Phase 0b chrome as "next", and recent commits are Phase 1 panel migrations. Polishing chrome around a gray untextured mesh is the wrong order. The phase covers §1's six criticals, gated by the Gate-0 journey test. Freeze GUI and P2 kills until it passes.
2. **[critical] Split ✓ into two states.** "✓ code" means the module exists and its tests pass. "✓ reachable" means the journey test or a recorded manual run shows a user reaching it. Only "reachable" counts toward the P0 floor. Re-audit all 57 P0 rows under this rule; my estimate is that 6-10 drop.
3. **[major] Stop P2 work while P0 has holes.**
   - PSD export (P2, §6:100) shipped while the viewport can't show paint.
   - The uncommitted `crates/umber-plugin-sdk/src/provider.rs` (1,118 lines, the P2 §10 AI provider interface) is in the tree now.
   - Fix: land or park provider.rs, then hold every remaining P2 row until the core-loop gate passes.
4. **[major] Make SPEC ratification and the dogfood gate hard prerequisites for the tag.** Both are written into SPEC.md (`:117`, `:65`) and were skipped under the autonomy grants. Add them to the release checklist as gates 6 and 7.
5. **[major] Re-sequence perf after the real data path exists.** The current baselines measure a 512² target, a texture-free viewport and metadata-only undo, so they will be invalidated by the core-loop phase. Re-baseline once the compositor and viewport binding land, and commit `perf/baseline.json` from that run.

---

## 5. VERDICT

**[critical] The P0/P1 completion claim is not honest as stated.** What's true is that the code for each row exists and passes isolated tests. The engine work (bakers, export, graph, UDIM math, the project JSON) is substantial and good.

What's false is that a user can do the P0 job. Six P0 rows are false on the main user path: viewport texturing, 4K, stroke undo, pixel persistence, pressure, and channel painting. Three more P0 rows (OCIO, stylus, distribution) are unmarked while STATE.md says "all 57 rows built." The contract every claim is measured against (SPEC v1.0) is still an unratified draft.

**Before calling v0.1.0 done:**
1. Land the core-loop phase: viewport texture binding, a per-layer/per-channel 4K tile pool with a GPU compositor, stroke undo, pixel save/load, and live pressure on Windows.
2. Add the Gate-0 journey test to the release checklist and pass it on both OSes, with a recording.
3. Resolve the three unmarked P0 rows (build them or formally re-tier them in DECISIONS.md), and fix the checklist's stale and contradictory lines.
4. Ratify the SPEC and run the dogfood gate with at least two external artists.
5. Re-run the perf baselines on the real data path, and commit `perf/baseline.json`.

Until steps 1-2 pass, v0.1.0 isn't a texture painter; it's a strong library set with a demo shell. Tagging it now would be the most damaging mistake available, because a texture-painting tool gets one first impression with artists.

---

I didn't edit any files, and I didn't touch the uncommitted plugin-sdk files. Two things I inferred but didn't open:
- Whether Phase 1 kill 1 actually landed layer thumbnails.
- Whether the fill layer writes into the same single per-tile target. Its module docs say it uses the same `WriteRegion` queue as retouch strokes.
